source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: This ACIAR-funded Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual (AH/2005/086) is written directly for Cambodian smallholder farmers, aiming to help them produce quality cattle that achieve the best market price. It frames cattle as an increasingly important store of wealth for smallholders -- used for income, draught power, and manure supply for fertilizer or bio-digestion -- and argues that as regional demand for beef and buffalo meat keeps growing in South-East Asia, reinvesting in better cattle health and nutrition is a sound strategy. The manual stresses that improving nutrition (especially through planted forages) both increases calf production and frees up family time otherwise spent on 'cut and carry' feed gathering, which in turn benefits children's time for school. It notes this is brief, high-level guidance and that farmers wanting more detail should consult their Village Animal Health Worker (VAHW) or District Veterinarian.
